hero.heading: What this component does
hero.description: The empty card shell, three stacked slots inside a bordered surface. It decides the surface, the border, the corner treatment and the fact that content is clipped to the frame, and nothing else. Header and Footer can each be switched off, Body is always present. Reach for a Card Template when you want a card already assembled, and for this when you are composing one yourself.

rows.Description: Square corners, matching surfaces and controls that are also square.
Softened corners, for a card that should read as a distinct object on the page. Content is clipped to the corner, so a full-bleed image inside follows the curve rather than squaring it off.
Shows the header slot above the body, for a title row or a heading with actions.
Hides the header slot along with anything placed in it. The body then meets the top edge, which is what a media-led card wants.
Shows the footer slot below the body, for the actions that close out the card.
Hides the footer slot and everything in it. Use when the card is purely informational and has nothing to act on.

rows.What changes: The shell has no interaction states. Hover, focus and selection all belong to whatever is placed in its slots, so the card itself never changes appearance.

rows.Description: Figma stores no timing and the shell models no transition. Showing or hiding a slot is a property change rather than something that animates here.
Width is fixed and height hugs the slots, so the card grows downward as content is added and never sideways.
The shell and all three slots clip their content. Anything larger than the card is cut at the edge rather than overflowing, which is what lets a full-bleed image sit flush inside a rounded corner.
A title row at the top, hidden by hasHeader. It ships empty, and _Card Heading is the part built for it.

The card's main content. It has no visibility toggle, so unlike the other two it cannot be switched off. _Card Body, _Card Image and _Card Heading are all offered, and the media templates stack several of them.
The actions that close out the card, hidden by hasFooter. _Card Footer carries the one, two and custom action arrangements.
Each slot uses a single property across both Shape variants, so switching Shape keeps whatever has been placed in them.

sections.title: Anatomy
rawTextContent: The outer frame. Fixed width, hugging height, carrying the surface, the border and the radius. It clips everything inside it.
The top slot, for a title row or a heading with actions. Switched off as a whole by hasHeader.
The middle slot and the card's main content. It is the one slot with no visibility toggle.
The bottom slot, for closing actions. Switched off as a whole by hasFooter.

sections.title: How to use
dos: Switch off the header for a media-led card, so the image meets the top edge rather than sitting under an empty row.
Let the card grow downward. Height hugs the slots, so adding content is safe in a way that widening it is not.
donts: Don't expect the card to widen for its content. Width is fixed, so a long unbroken string is clipped at the edge rather than pushing the card out.
Don't rely on Body being optional. It has no toggle, so a card with nothing to put there still reserves the space.

sections.title: Accessibility & Content Guidelines
items: The shell is a container and announces nothing itself. Whatever meaning the card carries comes from the parts placed in its slots.
Content is clipped at the card's edge, so text that overflows disappears rather than wrapping outside. Check long strings at the fixed width.
The card is not interactive here. If the whole card is meant to be clickable, that target and its focus treatment have to be built in code.
The border is the only thing separating the card from the page. Check border/default against the surface behind it.

rows.Description: 330px as drawn. The shell does not hug horizontally, so whoever places it decides the width.
Grows with the slots. With all three shown and empty it stands at 214px.
Zero on the shell and zero between the slots. Every inset comes from the parts placed inside, which is why an empty card reads as three touching bands.
radius/none when sharp, radius/sm when rounded. The shell clips to this radius, so inner content follows the curve.
1px (stroke/thin) on border/default, on all four edges, at both Shape values.
surface/card on the shell and on each of the three slots, so a slot left empty still reads as card surface rather than a hole.
No shadow at either Shape. The card sits flat and is separated from the page by its border alone.
